title: The 1787 text bars states from coining money and from ex post facto laws
summary: The 1787 text bars states from coining money and from ex post facto laws.
body: Article I, Section 10 of the 1787 transcription forbids states a list of acts, including treaties, coining money, emitting bills of credit, making anything but gold and silver coin a tender for debts, bills of attainder, ex post facto laws, and laws impairing the obligation of contracts. The source says: "No State shall enter into any Treaty, Alliance, or Confederation; grant Letters of Marque and Reprisal; coin Money; emit Bills of Credit; make any Thing but gold and silver Coin a Tender in Payment of Debts; pass any Bill of Attainder, ex post facto Law, or Law impairing the Obligation of Contracts, or grant any Title of Nobility." The list is a restraint written on the states. It is not a description of how every later court applied the contract clause.
